title: DiffTracker
description: A diff is one agent's set of edits to one file. It is a list of hunks. Each hunk says: which lines to target, what those lines currently say (before), and what to replace them with (after).

agent.description: Which agent produced this diff. Must be 1 or higher. The current Lean model requires only that it is positive; uniqueness between agents is a project-level convention, not a schema-enforced rule.

file.description: The path to the file being edited. Must not be empty. Example: 'hello.py' or 'src/main.lean'.

timestamp.description: When this diff was produced. Intended format: ISO 8601 date-time, for example '2026-04-21T10:00:00Z'. This field is required. The Lean side currently treats it as a required string and does not enforce the date-time syntax by itself.

base_line_count.description: How many lines the original file had before any edits. This field is required. The Lean application path uses it when a concrete base file is supplied, but JSON Schema alone cannot compare it against file contents.

diffs.description: The list of individual edits (called hunks). Each hunk targets a different part of the file. Across the whole diff, hunks must stay pairwise separated, and same-position inserts with different text are rejected by the Lean validator.

hunk.description: One edit operation: the target range, the old lines to match, and the new lines to write.

seq.description: The sequence number of this hunk within the diff. Starts at 1. Used for traceability and error messages. Lean execution order is determined by range sorting, not by seq.

op.description: The kind of edit. 'insert' adds new lines without removing any. 'delete' removes lines without adding any. 'replace' removes old lines and puts new lines in their place.

range.description: Which lines of the ORIGINAL file this hunk targets. Written as [start, stop]. Line numbers are 1-indexed. The interval is half-open: start is included, stop is excluded. So [2, 4] means lines 2 and 3. For an insert, start equals stop (e.g. [5, 5]) meaning 'insert before line 5'.

before.description: The exact lines from the original file that this hunk targets. These must match the actual file contents — if they do not match, the diff is rejected (this prevents editing the wrong place). For 'insert' this must be empty [] because no lines are being removed.

after.description: The new lines to put in place of the 'before' lines. For 'delete' this must be empty [] because nothing is being added.

allOf.description: Rule: range[0] must be <= range[1]. This is enforced by the application layer, not JSON Schema.

then.description: INSERT rule: before must be empty (nothing removed), after must have at least one line (something added).
DELETE rule: before must have at least one line (the lines being removed), after must be empty (nothing added).
REPLACE rule: before must have at least one line (what is being removed), after must have at least one line (what is being added).
